title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page completes the dictionary between combinatorial maps and the thrice-punctured sphere set up on the previous page. That page established Π03 ≅ π1(U_{0,3}, P_+), with U_{0,3} = P^1(C) \ {0,1,∞}, and identified isotopy classes of oriented, weighted ('pondérées') triangulated maps with finite Π03-sets. Here Grothendieck turns this into geometry.

(1) Covers. The category of weighted cellular triangulated maps is equivalent to that of surfaces that are (finite) ramified covers X → P^1(C), ramified at most over 0, 1, ∞. By the Riemann existence theorem such covers are canonically complete smooth algebraic curves over C.

(2) Recovering the map from the cover. The map K on X is the inverse image of the equator P^1(R). The vertices of type i ∈ {0,1,∞} form the fibre over i. The orders of the vertices are the ramification indices. The edges are the connected components of the inverse images of the open segments ]1,∞[, ]∞,0[ and ]0,1[.

(3) Ordinary maps. Barycentric subdivisions of ordinary (unweighted) maps correspond to the quotient by ρ1² = 1 (cf. Γ32^+ ≅ Π03/⟨ρ1²⟩ on the previous page). Such a map is recovered as the inverse image of [0,1]:
- vertices are the points over 0;
- edge midpoints are the points over 1;
- face centres are the points over ∞.
This is exactly the 'dessin d'enfant' convention.

(4) The universal map. The universal oriented map on P^1(C) is S_0 = {0} ⊂ K_∞ = [0,1]: one vertex, one edge, one face. The next page describes its barycentric subdivision (the equator divided into K_0, K_1, K_∞, with the hemispheres as the two oriented 'repères') as the universal oriented triangular map.

Purpose: to express the action of Π03 (and later its profinite completion and Gal(Q̄/Q)) on maps through covers of P^1 minus three points. This is the foundational dictionary of the dessins d'enfants programme in the Teichmüller/anabelian context.
errors: 'Ces revêtements sont des formes canoniques des courbes algébriques (propres et lisses) sur C' is loose. Such covers give a canonical algebraic structure (Riemann existence), but the curves arising are exactly those definable over Q̄ (Belyi), not arbitrary curves over C. This is not stated on this page.
A minor slip is corrected in the manuscript itself: the segment ]∞,1[ was rewritten as ]∞,0[.

ideas.what: Equivalence between (weighted triangulated / ordinary) maps and finite covers of P^1 unramified outside 0,1,∞, with the map as the inverse image of P^1(R) or of [0,1]
ideas.modern_name: Dessins d'enfants / Belyi pairs ↔ maps (Grothendieck correspondence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); anticipated by Jones–Singerman (1978) and Malgoire–Voisin (1977); arithmetic side by Belyi (1979)

ideas.what: Clean dessins / ordinary maps as the case ρ1²=1: vertices over 0, edge midpoints over 1, face centres over ∞
ideas.modern_name: Clean dessins; maps as quotients of the (2,∞,∞) or (∞,2,∞) triangle group / cartographic group

ideas.what: Universal map on P^1: S_0={0}, single edge [0,1], whose barycentric subdivision is the equator triangulation with hemispheres as the two triangles
ideas.modern_name: Universal (trivial) dessin; the two-triangle decomposition of the Riemann sphere
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in dessin literature (Jones–Singerman, Grothendieck, Schneps et al.)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early (1981) manuscript form of the standard dessins/maps ↔ Belyi covers dictionary later published in the Esquisse. It is of historical interest for dating, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'prédiées' is likely 'pondérées' (weighted, as on the previous page), followed by 'apparaissent comme équivalentes'.

'les ordres résiduels des sommets sont les pts de ramification' more plausibly reads 'les ordres des sommets sont les indices de ramification' (or similar). Trust the image; the sense is that vertex orders equal ramification indices.
'{+surfaces [?]+} des {+ramifiés+} revêtements' should read 'des revêtements ramifiés' (surfaces revêtements ramifiés).
